messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95/p99 latency alert on prod-inference-usw2. p95 > 600ms, p99 > 1500ms for /v1/chat/stream. autoscaling buckets trending unusual.
nora: paging @raj @kevin — streaming tail looks bad, customers seeing rebuffering. I see a spike in kv-cache evictions and prefiller OOMs.
raj: I'm on call. pulling KV metrics and pod logs. can you paste links to dashboards?
k
kevin: dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/latency?since=10m and kv cache: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-alloc?since=15m
nora: pasted logs from prefiller cluster: 
```
2026-03-15T20:01:04Z prefiller-7fc: ERROR: large alloc 2.1GB failed, falling back to fragmented arena
2026-03-15T20:01:05Z prefiller-7fc: WARN: fragmentation ratio=0.78
2026-03-15T20:01:05Z cache-shard-4: INFO: evicting 1024 entries, reclaimed=48MB
2026-03-15T20:01:06Z decoder-2a1: WARN: cache-miss, fetch-latency=420ms
2026-03-15T20:01:07Z router: detected streaming stall req=abcd-1234, retries=2
```
raj: eviction rate jumped from ~6/s to 140/s in 7m. prefill worker memory footprint shows many small free segments — allocator fragmentation. decode workers are starving for prefills. this aligns with prefill vs decode imbalance.
kevin: customer impact: support-bot flagged 6 accounts with >5% failed streams in the last 15m. severity: Sev2.
matt: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) apply backpressure at the gateway for sequences >2k tokens 2) reduce prefiller batch size and concurrency 3) enable per-shard soft-eviction hold for 3m to stop thrash 4) restart prefiller pods with compacting allocator enabled 5) emergency route: route 20% traffic to smaller 7b decode-only variant.
raj: agreed. I'll implement gateway throttling + routing. kevin, can you change prefiller concurrency?
kevin: changing prefiller settings now. running: 
```
rictl scale pool/prefill --concurrency 6 --region us-west-2
rictl config prefiller --batch-size 8 --enable-compact-allocator=true
```
nora: I pushed a temporary gateway rule to rate-limit long-seq POSTs: 
```
# nginx APIGW snippet added
if ($http_x_seq_len > 2048) {
  limit_req zone=longseq burst=20 nodelay;
}
```
ops-bot: ACTION: routing update: /v1/chat/stream => redwood-llama-7b-decode-only at 20% for seq_len>2048.
(2m later)
kevin: prefiller concurrency reduced, compact allocator flag flipped, restarting pods now: 
```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/prefiller
```
raj: monitoring: eviction rate falling: 140/s -> 32/s. kv hit-ratio improving 64% -> 82%. p99 dropping 1480ms -> 900ms. streaming stall count falling.
kevin: note: restart reclaimed fragmented heaps, compact allocator helped immediate reuse. but we saw increased CPU on prefiller during compaction. we should watch for CPU SLO impacts.
matt: customer comms: ETA around 25-40m. I've posted a short note to #support-customers and added targeted DMs to impacted accounts.
(10m later)
raj: metrics are stable for 7 minutes. p95 ~ 480ms, p99 ~ 650ms. eviction rate ~9/s. prefiller CPU up 12% but within autoscale headroom.
kevin: follow-up actions (post-incident):
- implement pooled arena allocator and unit tests to reproduce fragmentation patterns
- add an alert for prefiller fragmentation ratio > 0.6 and eviction > 50/s for 3m
- add gateway slow-path to automatically route to decode-only when hit-ratio < 70% for 2m
- evaluate eviction policy: better cross-shard LRU and avoid immediate global evictions under memory pressure
- run a stress job to reproduce large token-sequence churn before next release
raj: I'll file tickets and assign owners. starting a branch for allocator changes. kevin, please own the alerting PR.
kevin: ack. also adding a playbook note: when fragmentation detected, prefer throttling new large prefill requests before increasing shard memory.
nora: handing off to raj at 20:40 UTC. cluster marked stable but closely monitored.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity downgraded to Monitoring. PagerDuty incident remains open for postmortem.
support-bot: Notified customers that mitigations are in place; follow-up email scheduled after postmortem.
raj: summary for next oncall: cause: allocator fragmentation in prefiller led to eviction thrash and decode starvation, causing p95/p99 spikes and streaming stalls. immediate mitigations: throttle long seqs at gateway, reduce prefiller concurrency, enable compacting allocator, restart prefiller pods, route fraction of traffic to decode-only model. Next steps: allocator redesign, new alerts, runbook update: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-prefill-frag.
matt: handoff complete. ping thread for regressions. :raised_hands:
